images.title: Octagonal prism and pyramid
images.purpose: Compares the prism and the pyramid on the same octagon with their counts of faces, edges and vertices.
images.composition: Plain white background with generous empty margins; the main object is large and centred and fills about 60 percent of the frame; nothing else is drawn. Two solids side by side with clear space between: an octagonal prism on the left, an octagonal pyramid on the right, same octagon base size. A name above each and a three line count list below each.
images.exact_structure: Left: an upright prism with two congruent regular octagons (top and bottom) joined by 8 vertical edges; visible faces filled teal #0072B2, hidden edges dashed grey. Right: a pyramid on a regular octagon base with 8 edges rising to one apex; visible faces filled amber #E69F00, hidden edges dashed grey. Above left: 'octagonal prism'; above right: 'octagonal pyramid'. Below the prism, three lines: 'faces 10', 'edges 24', 'vertices 16'. Below the pyramid, three lines: 'faces 9', 'edges 16', 'vertices 9'.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: On the same 8 sided base the prism has n + 2, 3n, 2n parts and the pyramid n + 1, 2n, n + 1.
images.description: Compares the prism and the pyramid on the same octagon with their counts of faces, edges and vertices.
images.context: Concept T6.C4; one image that shows only the main idea.

image_decisions.why: A practice concept with no tool; a side by side comparison of the two solids on one base is its core check.
